name: physics_engine_mode
description: The contract Medhavy integrates against when the Physics Engine toggle is on. Analogous in placement to Google's AI Mode: a mode selector attached to the input, not a separate destination. The toggle's purpose is to make verification status visible to the student, so the single most important field in the response is `verification` -- not `answer`. An integration that renders the answer and drops the badge has removed the reason this mode exists.

query.description: The student's problem, as typed. Raw text; no pre-parsing required by the caller.

session_id.description: Required. Groups queries into a session for latency and engagement telemetry. NOT a student identifier.

student_id.description: Optional and currently unused by this mode. Only grade mode (Phase 2) needs it, and it must not be sent until the data processing agreement question (Q6 in the brief) is settled. The event log will reject student_id on any event not scoped to carry it.

render.description: solve returns the answer; tutor returns a progressive hint ladder and deliberately withholds the answer. Same underlying solution object, rendered differently -- per the brief's one-object-three-surfaces design. Grade mode is a separate pair of endpoints, not a render value: see `grade_mode` below.

problem_id.description: Optional stable id for traceability across logs.

verification.description: THE field to render. verified = a symbolic solver computed this and it is reproducible. needs_review = several physical principles fit and disagree; each candidate is computed correctly but choosing needs context. unverified = nothing in the formula library covers this, so no symbolic check happened.

badge.description: Human-readable label for the verification state, safe to show a student verbatim.

needs_llm_completion.description: True means this engine has done all it can and Medhavy's own model must write the final answer -- but must present it under the badge above, NOT as verified. This is the single field most likely to be misimplemented: treating it as 'fall back silently' reintroduces exactly the confidently-wrong-answer failure the engine exists to prevent.

answer.description: variable name -> numeric value. Null in tutor render (withheld on purpose) and on the needs_review / unverified routes.

candidates.description: Present only on needs_review. Each entry has principle, applies_when, and answer. Render all of them; picking one silently defeats the route.

hints.description: Present only in tutor render. Ordered ladder, each rung revealing more than the last, answer last. Reveal one at a time.

explanation.description: Plain-language account of what was done. Assembled from the card and the verify stage, not generated, so it cannot claim a check that did not run.

formula_used.description: Name of the physical principle applied. Worth surfacing -- it is most of why a student should believe the answer.

assumptions.description: Applicability conditions the matched formula assumes. Worth showing; several common wrong answers come from applying a formula outside its conditions.

sources.description: variable name -> the phrase in the student's own text it was read from. Enables 'we read 25 m/s from <this>' and makes a misparse traceable rather than mysterious.

route.description: Internal routing decision, for logs and debugging. Do not render to students.

formula_latex.description: The matched card's equations as LaTeX, one string per equation. Empty in tutor render (it would give the hints away) and when no card matched.

general_answer_latex.description: variable name -> LaTeX of the rearranged general formula, e.g. "T = \frac{2 g m_1 m_2}{m_1 + m_2}". Null in tutor render and when no card matched.

trace.description: Full solution object: every pipeline stage, verification checks, symbolic forms. For debugging and for the event log; not for the UI.

ui_guidance.verified: Show the answer with the badge. Surfacing formula_used and assumptions alongside is what makes it a verification tool rather than a fast calculator.
ui_guidance.needs_review: Show every candidate with its applies_when condition. This is a genuine teaching moment -- the student choosing between two principles based on their problem's context is the physics. Do not auto-pick.
ui_guidance.unverified: Medhavy's model answers normally, but the badge must be visible. This is the same answer quality as toggle-off; the badge is the only difference, and it is the whole point.
ui_guidance.never: Never render an unverified or needs_review answer under a verified badge. The engine cannot prevent that on the client side -- it is an integration invariant, and the reason needs_llm_completion is a required field.
ui_guidance.grade: Render the grade `badge` first, as for solve. Show per_quantity as right/wrong per value. Hide reference_answer and every per_quantity `reference` after the FIRST wrong attempt; show them after the second wrong attempt, or when the student asks. This is a UI rule only: the values are in the response, so it stops accidental spoilers, not a determined student. feedback never contains the correct value, so it is always safe to show.

grade_mode.description: Two steps. POST /parse reads the problem and says which quantities the student must answer, with labels and units, without the answer. POST /grade then checks the student's numbers. Passing /parse's `parsed` object to /grade means the problem is parsed once: one model call, and no risk of the second parse naming a quantity differently. Both need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Nothing is stored.

session_id.description: Same as /solve. Not a student identifier.

gradable.description: False when the engine has no single verified reference: no card matched, more than one principle fits, verification failed, or the problem is written in symbols.

reason.description: Plain-language reason when gradable is false. Safe to show a student.

unknowns.description: What the student must answer: [{name, label, unit}]. `name` is the key to use in student_answer; `label` and `unit` are for display. Empty when not gradable.

given.description: What the engine read from the problem: [{name, value, unit, added}]. `added` = a standard constant the student didn't state (e.g. g). Show it so a misread problem is caught before grading.

parsed.description: {knowns, unknowns, topic_hint}. Opaque to the UI: send it back to /grade unchanged. Null when not gradable.
From /parse. If missing, /grade parses `query` itself (one model call, and names may differ from an earlier parse).

student_answer.description: name -> number, for the names in /parse's `unknowns`. Numbers only: strings are rejected with 400.

verification.description: verified = graded against a symbolically verified reference. unverified = not graded (assessment is not_assessable).

badge.description: Label for the verification state, safe to show verbatim.

assessment.description: wrong_method = the wrong value matches a known mistake (see misconception). incomplete = every value given is right but some asked-for ones are missing.

per_quantity.description: name -> {submitted, reference, correct}, for each submitted asked-for quantity. `reference` is the correct value: see ui_guidance.grade.

reference_answer.description: name -> correct value, asked-for quantities only. See ui_guidance.grade.

reference_formula.description: Name of the principle the reference used.

divergence.description: Reserved for step-by-step grading. Not filled by the web UI yet.

misconception.description: Machine name of the matched mistake (sign_flip, reciprocal, factor_2_high, ...). For analytics; the readable version is in feedback.

missing.description: Asked-for names the student left out.

feedback.description: Plain-language result. Never contains the correct value.

grade_mode.errors: 400 = bad request body (message in `error`). 401 = bad token. 429 = rate limited (only a /parse, or a /grade without `parsed`, uses model quota). 503 = engine error; safe to retry.
